overview.text: Children's Python is a small, non-venomous python of northern Australia, named after the zoologist John George Children.

identification.text: Usually reddish-brown; its small smooth scales show a rainbow sheen in sunlight.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Northern Western Australia, the northern Northern Territory, northern Queensland and the Torres Strait islands.

habitat.text: Forest, savanna, shrubland, desert, grassland and wetlands; often in caves.

behaviour.text: Active at night; mostly on the ground but often climbs.

diet.text: Reptiles, birds and small mammals - especially small bats, which it catches by hanging from cave ceilings and grabbing them as they fly past.

funfacts.text: It hangs from the ceiling of a cave to snatch bats out of the air.

recognise.text: Small reddish-brown python with a rainbow sheen.
